chains.title: GATA2 site created by alt A at the TERT promoter

links.claim: Alt A is predicted to create a GATA2 consensus site at rs34768248, so GATA2 binds the alt allele more strongly than ref G. I choose GATA2 rather than GATA1/GATA3 because GATA2 is a plausible TERT-promoter regulator in glioblastoma and the G>A change fits a GATA-motif creation model; no QBiC-SELEX or ChIP evidence is supplied, so this is a motif-based claim only.
rs34768248 lies in the TERT promoter region upstream of the TERT transcription start site, where a gained GATA2 site could act as a promoter/enhancer element.
The element regulates TERT, the telomerase catalytic subunit gene.

The effect is expected in glioblastoma cells, and possibly melanoma and bladder cancer cells, where TERT promoter activity and GATA2 expression are relevant; DepMap glioblastoma is the supplied expression context.
Increased GATA2 binding at the alt allele is predicted to increase TERT expression, supporting telomere maintenance and cancer risk in glioblastoma, melanoma and bladder cancer.

predictions: Alt-specific GATA2 binding by EMSA or ChIP-qPCR over rs34768248.
Alt allele gives higher TERT reporter activity in glioblastoma cells.
GATA2 knockdown reduces the alt-allele-specific TERT effect.
falsified_if: GATA2 binds ref more than alt, or does not bind either allele.
No allele-specific TERT expression or reporter effect is observed.

chains.title: Null: no TF-mediated allelic effect at rs34768248
predictions: No reproducible allele-specific TF binding at rs34768248.
Any TERT or disease association is explained by a linked causal variant, a passenger event, or no allelic effect.
Reporter assays show no allele-specific difference after controlling for nearby variants.
falsified_if: A reproducible allele-specific TF occupancy and allele-specific TERT effect are demonstrated at rs34768248.

chains.title: GABPA/ETS site created by alt A at the TERT promoter

links.claim: Alt A is predicted to create or strengthen an ETS-family motif, so GABPA binds the alt allele more strongly than ref G. I choose GABPA over ETS1/ELK1 because TERT promoter ETS sites are commonly GABPA-bound and TERT promoter mutations often create ETS sites; no QBiC-SELEX or ChIP evidence is supplied, so this remains motif- and literature-based.
rs34768248 lies in the TERT promoter, where a gained ETS/GABPA site could modulate promoter activity.
The effect is expected in glioblastoma and other TERT-promoter-active cancers such as melanoma and bladder cancer.
Increased GABPA binding at the alt allele is predicted to increase TERT expression and support cancer risk.

predictions: Alt-specific GABPA binding by EMSA or ChIP-qPCR over rs34768248.
Alt allele gives higher TERT reporter activity.
GABPA knockdown reduces the alt-allele-specific TERT effect.
falsified_if: GABPA does not occupy the variant region or binds ref more than alt.
TERT expression is not allele-specific in the relevant cell type.

chains.title: SP1 site disrupted by alt A, lowering TERT

links.claim: Ref G is predicted to preserve a GC-box/SP1 site, so SP1 binds ref more strongly than alt A; alt A would disrupt SP1 binding. This is a lower-probability motif-based alternative because TERT promoters are GC-rich and SP1 is a known TERT activator, but no QBiC-SELEX or ChIP evidence is supplied.
rs34768248 lies in the TERT promoter, where loss of an SP1 site could reduce promoter activity.
The effect would be expected in glioblastoma and other TERT-expressing cancer cells.

Alt A is predicted to lower SP1-driven TERT expression; if alt is the risk allele, this chain requires TERT lowering to be oncogenic in the relevant context, which is not the usual TERT-promoter model and is therefore assigned low probability.

predictions: Ref-specific SP1 binding by EMSA or ChIP-qPCR.
Alt allele gives lower TERT reporter activity.
SP1 knockdown reduces the ref-allele-specific TERT effect.
falsified_if: SP1 binds alt more than ref or does not bind the region.
Alt allele increases rather than decreases TERT expression.

outcomes.outcome: no allele-specific band for any tested TF

next_experiment: Allele-specific EMSA with short probes spanning rs34768248 (G vs A) and recombinant GATA2 and GABPA, optionally with antibody supershift; this is the cheapest single experiment that separates C1 from C2. C1 predicts an alt-specific GATA2 shift; C2 predicts an alt-specific GABPA shift; C4 predicts no allele-specific shift.
